paper_title: A Coin Has Two Sides A Novel Detector-Corrector Framework for Chinese   Spelling Correction
caption: Proportion of correct corrections among various error detection results in SIGHAN15. "P" signifies the errors in high precision results, "R" signifies in high recall results, "N" signifies not been detected. The suffix "W" indicates cases where correction has failed.
model_annotation: The image displays two pie charts side by side, titled "All Changes" and "All Errors," illustrating the distribution of different types of error detection and correction outcomes in the context of Chinese spelling correction, as evaluated on the SIGHAN15 dataset. Both charts are segmented into six categories, each represented by a distinct color and labeled with a percentage value, with a shared legend on the right indicating the meaning of each color: light green for "P" (high precision errors), dark green for "PW" (high precision with failed correction), pale yellow for "R" (high recall errors), mustard yellow for "RW" (high recall with failed correction), light blue for "N" (not detected), and dark blue for "NW" (not detected with failed correction). In the "All Changes" chart, the largest segment is light green ("P") at 50%, followed by pale yellow ("R") at 26%, mustard yellow ("RW") at 14%, dark green ("PW") at 4%, dark blue ("NW") at 5%, and light blue ("N") at 1%. In the "All Errors" chart, the largest segment is again light green ("P") at 56%, followed by pale yellow ("R") at 29%, mustard yellow ("RW") at 6%, dark green ("PW") at 3%, dark blue ("NW") at 5%, and light blue ("N") at 1%. The charts visually emphasize that the majority of changes and errors fall into the "P" category, with "R" being the second most common, and "N" and "PW" being the least frequent. The "All Errors" chart shows a slightly higher proportion of "P" and "R" errors compared to "All Changes," suggesting that the detected errors are more concentrated in the high precision and high recall categories. Each slice is labeled with its percentage, and the slices are arranged in a clockwise order starting from the top-right, with no explicit ordering by size.
